## Mathematical construction

The design inventory is preserved verbatim (`def-root-datum-of-split-reductive-group`, `thm-root-subgroups-…`, `thm-bruhat-decomposition-…`, `thm-parabolics-and-levi-decomposition`; `ex-root-groups-and-bruhat-cells-for-sl2`, `ex-standard-parabolics-in-gl-n`, `cex-lie-root-system-does-not-record-full-root-datum`). Because Milne's proofs of 21.11/21.68/21.80/21.91 rest on Chapters 13–20, I added the genuinely used local interfaces on the same A page: character/cocharacter lattices of a split torus, concentrator/limit subgroups (Ch. 13), weight subgroups attached to semigroups (Ch. 16), Cartan/Chevalley centralizer theory (Ch. 17), the rank-one classification (Ch. 20), plus the lattice root-datum combinatorics (App. C). Two dependency cycles found during construction were removed by restructuring `def-parabolic-…` and `def-radical-…`; no cycle remains. 27 items declare Choice explicitly; 4 are choice-free.

## Source gate

The design's **second-source gate is closed** by reading Conrad, *Reductive Group Schemes* (Thm. 1.4.12 Bruhat via BN-pairs, Thms. 4.1.4/4.1.7 dynamic method, Lemma 4.2.2/Thm. 4.2.6, Prop. 5.1.6) and Herzig, *Linear Algebraic Groups* (Thms. 130/136/146/157, Cor. 158, Props. 171/174, Thm. 178/180). Residual limitations (Milne-only graded-Nakayama and concentrator-glueing lemmas; Milne 20.33 classification not needed and recorded `deferred → owner-decision`) are stated honestly in the notes rather than overclaimed.
